copy_pick.why: Candidate 2's 'MINES CLAIM THREE SHIPS' best fits the wire-service deadpan, steers clear of the 10-30 'FOUR TANKERS... HORMUZ' shape and the recent 'which is one way to' and 'bold' echoes, and its summary makes one sharp point: the war is leaking into London and DC zip codes.

doom.driver: Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz will stay shut until demands are met. Mohsen Rezaei's comments come as the IRGC said at least three ships had hit mines and caught fire in the Hormuz strait.
doom.summary: Three ships burning on IRGC mines, a Treasury Secretary relocated to a military base because Tehran found his house on the internet, and an alleged Iran-backed plot near RAF Fairford: the war is now leaking into London and DC zip codes. Meanwhile Congo's Ebola count blew past 11,000 and Google released an agent swarm to the public, because apparently today needed more swarming things.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Gemini 4 Carbon goes public with agent swarms, and AlphaProof Code and Gemini Robotics 2.5 round out a heavy DeepMind week.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: A US-China AI dialogue and a regulation-minded Wiener headed to Congress amount to paperwork, not guardrails.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Hormuz stays shut and mined, Iran-linked plots surface in the UK, and Russia-Ukraine talks produce four hours of nothing.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: A new robot jailbreak benchmark, leaky Grok Build apps and AI-faked 911 calls show the misuse surface growing.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: A US soldier is accused of spying for Russia in London while investors bunker into defensive stocks.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. A wide aerial view looking down at a 45-degree angle over the eastern Strait of Hormuz, rendered as a vast molten landscape. The water is a sheet of glowing furnace-orange crude with blood-red ripples, and a hellish glare rises from it to light everything from below. On the left, the jagged tan-grey limestone cliffs of Oman's Musandam Peninsula plunge into the channel, their fjord inlets lit orange with bruised-violet shadow faces. A tiny fishing village of flat-roofed huts clings to a cove, and its windows glow. On the right, the low red-ochre, salt-streaked islands of Hormuz and Qeshm sit in a hazy crimson mist, with the Iranian mainland coast behind them. Spanning the whole narrow channel from cliff to island is a colossal rust-pitted iron chain, its links as big as houses, sagging just above the water. At its center hangs a giant black iron padlock, the size of a city block, clamped shut. A huge brass key is jammed in its keyhole, snapped off halfway and glinting gold-orange. Around the chain, black spiked naval mines with rusted horns bob in the glowing water. Each is ringed by a small burning slick, and together they form a menacing scatter across the strait. Thick black-violet smoke columns rise from two of the slicks into a blood-red sky streaked with furnace-orange cloud. On a lit ledge of the Musandam cliff, a few tiny whole figures stand in silhouette, dwarfed by the lock and looking out at it. No ships are visible, and the whole frame is vivid and fully readable.

minor: The chain on the left runs along and merges into the cliff face rather than clearly spanning from the cliff over the water, so its anchor point is a bit muddled.
The chain's right end curls into a loop on the island and ends abruptly, not reading as a clean attachment.
The padlock sits on the water rather than hanging from the chain, and the key is small and a little hard to read as snapped off.
The right-hand islands are flat, striated terraces that look more like stepped sand dunes than salt-streaked islands, and the Iranian mainland is hard to make out.
The tiny figures on the left ledge are very small and blobby, but they read as silhouettes.
The fishing village is barely visible; the cliff has glowing cave openings instead of obvious huts.
The mines are fairly evenly scattered and similar in size, which looks repetitive.

dawn.driver: Vinícius Jr sends message to Sudan boy who received prosthetic legs after BBC report sparks appeal. Double amputee Zaher told the BBC last year about his favourite footballer and a dream of being able to walk again.
dawn.blurb: ON NEW LEGS, YOUNG ZAHER RISES
dawn.summary: Zaher told the BBC last year that he dreamed of walking again and loved Vinícius Jr. Viewers answered with an appeal that got him prosthetic legs, and now his hero has sent him a personal message. In Trinidad and Tobago, Jason Jones won his 11-year legal fight as the court overturned the country's anti-homosexuality laws. And four NASA volunteers stepped out after more than a year in a simulated Mars habitat, where they grew their own food and learned lessons for future crews on the Moon and Mars.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Astronomers built a digital twin of the James Webb Space Telescope to strip away starlight glare, making faint exoplanets two to 15 times easier to spot, and found a hidden world with it.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Volunteers with Musicians On Call are bringing live music to the bedsides of hospitalized veterans.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: A boy who dreamed of walking again now has prosthetic legs, thanks to strangers who answered his story, and a message from his football hero.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall in 2026 as renewable energy and electric vehicles gain ground.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Fossils from Thailand reveal Yakamys sirindhornae, a 66-pound rodent from 34 million years ago that shows giant rodents evolved far earlier than anyone knew.

copy_pick.why: Its blurb 'ON NEW LEGS, YOUNG ZAHER RISES' matches the directive's quiet nature-documentary form, names the boy at the heart of a genuine small miracle, avoids repeating recent cards (unlike Candidate 3, which echoes the recent Hungary LGBTQ card), and stays purely on good news.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. WEATHER-DOMINATED scene of a flat concrete rooftop in a crowded Cairo neighborhood where Sudanese families have settled, seen through thick, glowing morning haze. Warm amber mist fills the whole frame and softens everything beyond the rooftop edge into layered silhouettes: stacked brick apartment blocks with forests of satellite dishes, a distant minaret, and a few palm tops fading into the golden fog. Clean low sun burns through the haze and lifts the shadows, with soft green and amber tones throughout. In the foreground, rooftop planters of mint and leafy green plants hold glistening dew. A white football jersey with a crest-like emblem and no readable lettering hangs on a laundry line, backlit and glowing in the sun. A worn football rests on the concrete. Near it, a Sudanese boy of about thirteen stands tall and smiling on two sleek prosthetic legs, shown whole and dignified, wearing a white jersey. His mother stands beside him in a flowing sage-green headscarf and robe, one hand on his shoulder. Two other children in the mid-ground kick a second ball through the drifting mist. The mood is hopeful and tender: shadows lifting, clarity arriving.

minor: The boy's prosthetic legs are thin, dark and a little robotic. They read as prosthetics, and the legs and boots connect cleanly to his shorts.
The crest and swoosh-like marks on both jerseys are tiny and unreadable. They work as stand-ins for a logo, not as lettering.
The two children in the mid-ground are soft, hazy silhouettes with simplified limbs. This fits the haze and distance.
The mother's hand on the boy's shoulder is slightly blocky, but it connects to her arm and reads correctly.
The pixel dithering and heavy amber grade lower the contrast on the background buildings. This is intentional.
